title: CRLR/839/2023 of SRI LAXMAN SINGH RANA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 839 of 2023
Sri Laxman Singh Rana ....Revisionist

Present:-
 Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, Advocate for the revisionist.
 Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, A.G.A. for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to an
order dated 19.08.2023, passed in Misc. Case No. 61 of
2020, Kiran Rana Vs. Laxman Singh Rana, by the court
of Additional Judge, Family Court, Rishikesh, Dehradun
("the case"). By it, the revisionist has been directed to pay
Rs.8,000/- per month, as interim maintenance to the
respondent no.3, the daughter of the parties.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. The respondent no.2 filed an application
under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 claiming maintenance from the revisionist which

2
is basis of the case. In the case, an application for
interim maintenance has also been filed.
4. It has been case of the respondent no.2 that
she and the revisionist were married on 16.11.2010.
They were blessed with a baby girl on 14.09.2010. But
thereafter, the revisionist and his family members ill-treated the respondent no.2. She was pressurised to
deliver a baby boy, but she was not given proper
treatment. She could not conceive thereafter. She was
finally expelled from her the matrimonial home on
04.06.2020. She is not able to maintain herself.
Whereas, the revisionist works in Electricity
Department and gets Rs.56,740/- salary per month.
He also runs a resort. His total income is more than
Rs.2 Lakh per month.
5. The revisionist objected to the application for
interim maintenance, inter alia, on the ground that on
25.08.2020, it is the respondent no.2, who herself left her
matrimonial house after taking the fight with the mother
of the revisionist.
6. The revisionist has admitted that he works in
the Electricity Department and has claimed the

3
respondent no.2 works as a Teacher and she has
concealed her income, which she derives from other
sources, as well.
7. The court below discussed the rival contentions
of the parties. Detailed discussion has been made on the
means of the parties. The court had taken note of the fact
that the respondent no.2 is working in the school and was
getting Rs.8,000/- to Rs. 10,000/- per month salary. The
court has also taken into consideration the admitted fact
that the revisionist works with the Electricity Department
and he has ancestral and other self acquired properties
also. The gross salary which is reflected by the revisionist
is more than Rs.74,000/- per month with other
deductions.
8. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that since the respondent also works as a Teacher
and has income from other sources also. She is LIC Agent
and also agent of Star Health Medicare Insurance from
which she derives huge income. But, it has not been
accepted by the court below. It is argued that need of a
child should be assessed first and whatever amount was
to be fixed for maintaining the girl child, it should have

4
been apportioned between the revisionist and the
respondent no.2 in proportion to their income.
9. It is a revision. The scope is quite restricted to
the extent of examining the legality, correctness and
propriety of the impugned judgment and order.
10. The impugned order is an order of interim
maintenance. The rights of the parties have not been
finally determined by the court below. The main
contention of the revision is that the income of the
respondent no.2 from the Health Insurance Agency as
well as from the LIC has not been considered. The
respondent no.2 has denied of having an income from the
LIC or from Heath Insurance Agency. It has been her
version that the revisionist would get her signatures on
various papers and he only runs those agencies and
maintains the accounts, the respondent no.2 has no
knowledge of those agencies, their income or accounts.
11. After considering those rival contentions, the
court in the impugned judgement has observed that with
regard to the income of the respondent no.2 from LIC or
Health Insurance Agency may only be determined after
parties adduce evidence. This Court does not find any

5
illegality or incorrectness in this finding. These are factual
aspects, which would find determination once parties
adduce their evidence.
12. One of the contentions of learned counsel for
the revisionist is that first and foremost, the need of the
child ought to have been assessed and then amount is to
be apportioned. In fact, that is the manner in which the
maintenance is awarded to a child. First and foremost,
the need of the child is assessed, thereafter, that amount
of maintenance, which a child deserves to get is
apportioned between the parents, in proportion to their
income. It has not been done in this case.
13. The question is should the Court remand this
case for this purpose? The answer is in negative for the
following reasons:-
(i) The court below did not record any finding
with regard to the income of the
respondent no.2 from the Health Care
Agency or the LIC on the ground that it is
disputed question of fact, which may find
determination after parties lead their
evidence.

6
(ii) The court below has assessed the income
of the respondent no.2 between
Rs.8,000/- to Rs.10,000/- by Teaching
profession.
(ii) Admittedly, the gross salary of the
revisionist is about Rs.74,000/- per
month.
14. If a wife does some work for her existence, the
law is that she may not be denied benefit of the
maintenance, so as to lead a life commensurate with the
financial and social status of her husband. Against more
than Rs.74,000/- per month gross salary of the
revisionist, the total money which the respondent no.2
would have, if the impugned order is not disturbed, is
Rs.18,000/- per month (Rs.10,000/- per month income of
the respondent no.2 and Rs.8000/- per month
maintenance awarded by the impugned order). This
amount Rs.18,000/- per month is for the maintenance of
the respondent no.2 the wife as well as the daughter.
Admittedly, the gross salary of the revisionist is more
than Rs.74,000/- per month. By virtue of the impugned
order the respondent no.2 would get Rs. 8,000/- per
month for maintaining her child, the respondent no.3. As

7
stated, she may have total Rs.18,000/- per month, with
her for maintaining herself and her child the respondent
no.3. Accordingly, the revisionist will be left about
Rs.66,000/- per month after payment of Rs.8,000/- per
month for the maintenance of the respondent no.3.
Therefore, merely because in the impugned order, the
amount that is needed to the respondent no.3, for her
maintenance, has not been calculated and such amount
has not been apportioned, the impugned order does not
warrant any interference.
15. Therefore, having considered the entirety of
facts, this Court is of the view that the impugned order
does not warrant any interference. Accordingly, the
revision deserves to be dismissed.
16. The revision is dismissed accordingly.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 10.06.2024
Jitendra
